Caves and geological landmarks

Caves and landmarks are not on every hill or valley. This page covers where caves open, the three cave layouts, and the landmark sites you can find in the base game.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 3 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides
Contents
  1. Hillside caves
  2. Geological landmarks
  3. How this was checked

Hillside caves

A cave is one bounded site. Every passage stays within about 132 m of the cave's centre, so it is not a deep network of tunnels. There is at most one cave in each 384 m square, and none within about 240 m of the world's origin. Hillside caves

A cave needs a hill at least 32 m above sea level. Its entrance is cut into the hillside about 100 m from the cave's centre, on ground at least 10 m above sea level. Caves are shallow: the floor never runs more than about 11 m below the ground at the entrance. In worlds made with the current generator, the entrance opens at ground level so you can walk in.

Each cave uses one of three layouts:

  • Fork and chamber: a central chamber with passages that branch off it.
  • Loop: two routes go around a solid rock mass and meet again.
  • Pillared hall: a broad, high hall held up by four rock pillars.

Floors climb in walkable half-metre steps. A cave ambience plays when you are more than 2 m below the ground with rock above you.

In caves cut through limestone, worlds made with the current generator have limestone stalagmites and stalactites in the high chambers, some joined into columns. They stay clear of the walking routes.

Good to know. Caves do not show on the map. They have no lights of their own. The rock is ordinary underground rock, so plain stone walls can hold the odd Iron ore block, as anywhere underground.
Planned, not in the game. Planned, not in the game yet: deeper cave networks and cave maps.

Geological landmarks

Landmarks are rare sites that spread 220 to 320 m out from their centre, so a whole site is about 440 to 640 m across. There is at most one in each 2 km square. They form only where the centre stands at least 20 m above sea level, not on water or lakes, not within 512 m of the world's origin and not on very rugged ground. Landmarks: meteor craters, amethyst gorges, lava tubes and other geological…

The ground decides which site you find:

  • Meteor crater: a main bowl about 185 to 270 m across and 20 to 30 m deep, with a raised rim and two smaller craters beside it. The ground is scorched stone and impact glass, with meteorite rocks of Iron ore and Impact glass. Only on ground that is not volcanic.
  • Amethyst gorge: a winding canyon 24 to 54 m deep, about 70 to 120 m across at the top, with a floor 15 to 25 m wide. Its dark stone is studded with Amethyst blocks and crystal clusters.
  • Lava tube: a walkable, roofed passage about 15 m below the ground, up to 8 m high and 16 m wide, with two open skylights. Only on volcanic ground.
  • Geyser basin and hot-spring terraces: only on volcanic ground.
  • Cold uplands: ice spires, moraine ridges, outwash plains and firn domes.
  • Warm, wet ground: karst towers and tepui mesas. Warm, dry ground: spring oases.
  • Other ground: granite domes, limestone pavements and slate quarries.
Good to know. Worlds made before the game recorded generator versions (Legacy worlds) have no landmark sites.

Sites are rare. Most of the map has none. To head for one, search the map locator for Meteor field, Amethyst gorge or Surface lava tubes; the other sites are listed under their biome names, such as Geyser basin or Tepui plateau.
